<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Dear Shareholder </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">On 22&nbsp;February 2011,
BHP Billiton announced an off-market tender buy-back (Buy-Back) of BHP Billiton Limited shares with a target size of A$5 billion to commence immediately. It forms an important part of the recently announced US$10 billion expanded capital management
program. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Our on-market buy-back of BHP Billiton Plc shares, which was reactivated in November 2010, forms the other component of this program
and will largely continue during the Buy-Back process. It is our expectation, subject to market conditions, that the expanded capital management program will be largely completed by the end of the 2011 calendar year. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Further information on how to participate and tender your shares into the Buy-Back is described below, with full details contained in this booklet.

shareholders. On completion, BHP Billiton will have repurchased approximately US$23 billion of BHP Billiton Limited and BHP Billiton Plc shares since 2004, representing about 15&nbsp;per cent of then issued capital.</FONT><FONT

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="tx157732_3"></A>1 Details of the Buy-Back and tender process </B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="font-size:12px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="line-height:2px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:2px;border-bottom:2pt solid #000000">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>This section sets out the terms of the Buy-Back and other information to assist you in making a decision whether to participate in the Buy-Back. You should also have regard to other information
previously made available to you about BHP Billiton, such as BHP Billiton&#146;s Results for the Half Year Ended 31&nbsp;December 2010 and the announcement regarding BHP Billiton&#146;s agreement to acquire all of Chesapeake Energy
Corporation&#146;s interests in the Fayetteville Shale, USA, which can be reviewed online at </B><I></I><B><I>www.bhpbilliton.com.</I></B><I></I><B> </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="font-size:12px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="line-height:2px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:2px;border-bottom:2pt solid #000000">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="font-size:12px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P><DIV STYLE="position:relative;float:left; margin-right:1%; width:48%;padding-right:9px;padding-bottom:8px;overflow:hidden">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="tx157732_4"></A>1.1 What is an off-market buy-back tender? </B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">An off-market buy-back tender involves a company inviting eligible shareholders to offer to sell some or all of their shares to the company by way of a
tender process. The shares bought back are subsequently cancelled, thereby reducing the total number of shares the company has on issue. Under the Buy-Back, Shares may be tendered by eligible BHP Billiton Limited shareholders at any of the specified
discounts in the Tender Discount range of between 10&nbsp;per cent and 14&nbsp;per cent inclusive (at 1&nbsp;per cent intervals) to the Market Price or as a Final Price Tender. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="tx157732_5"></A>1.2 Why is BHP Billiton implementing the Buy-Back? </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">As part of its
December 2010 Interim Results, BHP Billiton announced an expanded US$10 billion capital management program. The program will be executed in the form of both on-market buy-backs of BHP Billiton Plc shares and an off-market buy-back of BHP Billiton
Limited shares. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The off-market buy-back of BHP Billiton Limited shares has a target size of A$5 billion. BHP Billiton Limited may, at its
discretion, vary the size of the off-market buy-back. BHP Billiton Limited also retains the discretion to repurchase a lesser amount of shares than indicated or no shares at all. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The on-market buy-back of BHP Billiton Plc shares that was reactivated in November 2010 will continue, including largely over the period of the Buy-Back process. Subject to market conditions, it is BHP
Billiton&#146;s expectation that the US$10 billion capital management initiative will be largely completed by the end of the 2011 calendar year. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="font-size:12px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;
</FONT></P></DIV><DIV STYLE="position:relative;float:right; width:48%;padding-right:9px;padding-bottom:8px;overflow:hidden">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px;padding-bottom:0px;"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The announcement continues BHP Billiton&#146;s strong track record of returning excess
capital to shareholders. On completion of the US$10 billion capital management initiative, BHP Billiton will have repurchased approximately US$23 billion of BHP Billiton Limited and BHP Billiton Plc shares since 2004, representing 15&nbsp;per cent
of then issued capital.</FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="1"><SUP STYLE="vertical-align:baseline; position:relative; bottom:.8ex">1</SUP></FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"> </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Undertaking both an off-market and on-market buy-back, coupled with an increased interim dividend allows the entire BHP Billiton global shareholder base
to participate, both directly and indirectly, in the expanded capital management initiative. An off-market buy-back provides an efficient means of generating economic value for all BHP Billiton shareholders. The target Buy-Back size of A$5 billion
will enable BHP Billiton to continue to pay fully franked dividends under its progressive dividend policy. Further information about the effect of the Buy-Back on BHP Billiton is set out in Section&nbsp;3. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="tx157732_6"></A>1.3 What are the advantages of an off-market tender process? </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">BHP Billiton Limited is conducting the Buy-Back by way of a tender process. The advantages of the tender process include the following: </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="font-size:6px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Both participating and non-participating BHP Billiton shareholders are expected to benefit from the Buy-Back as: </FONT></P></TD></TR></TABLE>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">BHP Billiton Limited shareholders should not have to pay any brokerage to sell their Shares into the Buy-Back. </FONT></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="tx157732_7"></A>1.4 Did BHP Billiton consider other ways of returning capital? </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Board has considered various ways to return surplus capital to shareholders, including off-market buy-backs, on-market buy-backs, special dividends and a combination of these options. The Board
considers that, at this time, it is in the best interests of BHP Billiton and its shareholders as a whole to pursue an off-market buy-back of BHP Billiton Limited shares as part of BHP Billiton&#146;s expanded capital management program. The
benefits of the Buy-Back are discussed in Section&nbsp;1.3 above. </FONT></P></DIV><DIV STYLE="position:relative;float:right; width:48%;padding-right:9px;padding-bottom:8px;overflow:hidden">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Board believes that returning surplus capital to shareholders through an off-market share buy-back is
an important component of its strategy that aims to maximise economic value across BHP Billiton&#146;s entire shareholder base. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Buy-Back
is expected to enhance earnings per share and cash flow per share to a greater extent than a special dividend. In contrast, a special dividend only provides a discrete, one-off cash benefit to shareholders and offers no choice of participation. In
addition, a special dividend would need to be paid to all shareholders of BHP Billiton Limited and BHP Billiton Plc, and this mechanism is not considered to be the most efficient way to return capital to shareholders. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">While the precise impact of the Buy-Back cannot be determined, it is expected to have a lasting and positive impact on BHP Billiton&#146;s earnings per
share, cash flow per share and return on equity. As a result, all BHP Billiton shareholders will benefit. The Buy-Back will enable the purchase of BHP Billiton Limited Shares at a material discount to the prevailing market price of BHP Billiton
Limited and can be completed in a shorter period of time than on-market buy-backs of a comparable size. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="tx157732_8"></A>1.5 Am I
entitled to tender Shares into the Buy-Back? </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">If you are eligible to participate, you are entitled to tender up to 100&nbsp;per cent of the
Shares which are registered in your name on the Buy-Back Record Date (Thursday, 3&nbsp;March 2011). Shares acquired on the ASX on or after the ex-entitlement date (Friday, 25&nbsp;February 2011) generally will not be registered in your name by the
Buy-Back Record Date and therefore will not carry an entitlement to participate in the Buy-Back. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The maximum number of Shares you are
entitled to tender into the Buy-Back is set out in Box A on your personalised Tender Form enclosed with this booklet. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">If you hold 125 Shares
or less, and you wish to tender Shares in the Buy-Back, you must tender all of your Shares at the same Tender Discount or as a Final Price Tender.
</FONT></P></DIV><div style="clear:both; height:0px; font-size:0px">&nbsp;</div>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px;padding-bottom:0px;"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>1. Details of the Buy-Back and tender process </B><B><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="1">continued </FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"></FONT></B><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B> </B></FONT></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="font-size:12px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="line-height:2px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:2px;border-bottom:2pt solid #000000">&nbsp;</P> <p STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<DIV STYLE="position:relative;float:left; margin-right:1%; width:48%;padding-right:9px;padding-bottom:8px;overflow:hidden">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">If you hold more than 125 Shares, you may tender different parcels of your Shares set out in Box A on your
personalised Tender Form at one or more Tender Discounts or as a Final Price Tender. However, you must tender a minimum of 125 Shares in aggregate. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Buy-Back Invitation is not being made to any Excluded Foreign Person. In particular, the Buy-Back Invitation is not being made to any person in the United States or any US Person or resident of
Canada. ADRs and Restricted Employee Shares may not be tendered into the Buy-Back. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="tx157732_9"></A>1.6 How does the Buy-Back
compare to selling my Shares on the stock market? </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Depending on your individual circumstances, if you sell your Shares on the ASX, the
Australian tax consequences of doing so may be different from selling your Shares into the Buy-Back (see Section&nbsp;2 for general details in relation to Australian tax implications, but note that BHP Billiton Limited shareholders should consider
their own particular tax circumstances). </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In addition, to execute a share sale on the ASX, you will need to appoint a broker and may have to
pay brokerage whereas you should not need to appoint a broker or pay brokerage to sell your Shares into the Buy-Back. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">However, it is likely
that you will be able to sell your Shares on the ASX for a price that is higher than the Buy-Back Price. This is because the prices at which eligible BHP Billiton Limited shareholders can tender Shares into the Buy-Back are at discounts of between
10&nbsp;per cent and 14&nbsp;per cent inclusive to the Market Price. Therefore, it is likely that the BHP Billiton Limited share price on the ASX will be higher than the Buy-Back Price during and possibly immediately after the Tender Period.
</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">To provide eligible BHP Billiton Limited shareholders with an indication of the possible after-tax proceeds from selling their Shares into
the Buy-Back compared to selling their Shares on the ASX, BHP Billiton Limited intends to provide access to a tax calculator through its website <B>(</B><B><I>www.bhpbilliton.com</I></B><B>)</B> from approximately 7&nbsp;March 2011 to 18&nbsp;April
2011. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">By making the Buy-Back Invitation and setting the range of Tender Discounts, BHP Billiton Limited is not making any recommendation or
giving any advice on the value of your Shares or whether (or how) you should sell your Shares. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Before you decide whether to participate in
the Buy-Back, BHP Billiton Limited strongly recommends that you seek your own professional advice.
</FONT></P></DIV><DIV STYLE="position:relative;float:right; width:48%;padding-right:9px;padding-bottom:8px;overflow:hidden">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="tx157732_10"></A>1.7 Will I receive the 2011 interim dividend if my Shares are bought back?
</B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Yes. All shareholders with an entitled registered holding of shares in BHP Billiton Limited on Friday, 11&nbsp;March 2011 will be paid the
US 46 cents per share fully franked dividend in respect of that holding, whether or not they participate in the Buy-Back. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="tx157732_11">
</A>1.8 Do I have to tender my Shares? </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Participation in the Buy-Back is entirely at your discretion. You do not have to tender your Shares
if you do not want to. If you do not wish to participate, you do not have to take any action. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="tx157732_12"></A>1.9 What does the
Buy-Back mean for me if I do not participate? </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">If you choose not to participate, you are an Excluded Foreign Person or your Tender is
unsuccessful, the number of Shares you hold will not change as a result of the Buy-Back. After the Buy-Back is completed, you will hold a slightly larger percentage of the total shares in BHP Billiton (as there will be fewer shares on issue).
</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="tx157732_13"></A>1.10 What price will BHP Billiton Limited pay to buy back my Shares? </B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">BHP Billiton Limited will pay you the Buy-Back Price for each of your Shares accepted under the Buy-Back even if your Tender Discount is equal to or
larger than the Buy-Back Discount. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Buy-Back Price will be the price that equates to the largest Tender Discount in the range of between
10&nbsp;per cent and 14&nbsp;per cent inclusive (at 1&nbsp;per cent intervals) to the Market Price that will enable BHP Billiton Limited to purchase the amount of capital it determines to buy back. </FONT></P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px;padding-bottom:0px;"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">So, for example, if the relevant Market Price is A$45.00 and the Buy-Back Discount is

determine for Australian tax purposes the market value of the relevant Shares when the Buy-Back occurs. The Tax Value will be A$46.55, adjusted for the movement in the BHP Billiton Plc share price from the close of trading on the London Stock
Exchange on Monday, 21&nbsp;February 2011 to the opening of trading on the London Stock Exchange on the Closing Date (expected to be Friday, 8&nbsp;April 2011). If the movement in the BHP Billiton Plc share price is significantly different from the
movement in the BHP Billiton Limited share price over the relevant period, BHP Billiton Limited may approach the ATO to seek to vary the methodology used to determine the Tax Value. The method for determining the Tax Value is explained in more
detail in Section&nbsp;2.3. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="tx157732_14"></A>1.11 How will I know what the Market Price is? </B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Market Price is calculated as the volume weighted average price (VWAP) of BHP Billiton Limited shares over the five trading days up to and including
the Closing Date (excluding certain trades &#150; see definitions of VWAP and Market Price in Section&nbsp;5.1 for further details). </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">To
provide an indication of the Market Price, BHP Billiton Limited will calculate and make available to eligible shareholders the running VWAP during this five-day period. The running VWAP will be made available to eligible shareholders on BHP
Billiton&#146;s website from approximately 6.00pm (Melbourne time) on Monday, 4&nbsp;April 2011 <B>(</B><I></I><B><I>www.bhpbilliton.com</I></B><I></I><B>)</B> and will be available through the Buy-Back enquiry line from Tuesday, 5&nbsp;April 2011
and will be updated cumulatively each day. Please note that the Market Price information provided by BHP Billiton on its website and through the Buy-Back enquiry line will only be an estimate given that it is a cumulative daily update from the
opening of trading on Monday, 4&nbsp;April 2011. </FONT></P></DIV><DIV STYLE="position:relative;float:right; width:48%;padding-right:9px;padding-bottom:8px;overflow:hidden">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The actual Market Price, representing the VWAP for the full five-day period up to and including the Closing
Date, will be available from approximately 6.00pm (Melbourne time) on Friday, 8&nbsp;April 2011, and can be obtained by accessing the BHP Billiton website or by calling the Buy-Back enquiry line on 1300 612 584 within Australia, 0800 451 521 within
New Zealand or &#43;61 3 9415 4868 if you are calling from outside Australia or New Zealand. BHP Billiton Limited also intends to announce the Market Price to the ASX (and other relevant exchanges) as soon as practicable on Friday, 8&nbsp;April
2011. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="tx157732_15"></A>1.12 What is a Final Price Tender? </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">A Final Price Tender is an offer to sell your Shares to BHP Billiton Limited at whatever price is ultimately determined to be the Buy-Back Price under the tender process. The Buy-Back Price could be as
low as a 14&nbsp;per cent discount to the Market Price or as high as a 10&nbsp;per cent discount to the Market Price. If a large number of Final Price Tenders are submitted, it is more likely that the Buy-Back Price will be at a larger discount to
the Market Price subject to the 14&nbsp;per cent maximum. Final Price Tenders are designed to make it easier for eligible BHP Billiton Limited retail shareholders to participate successfully in the Buy-Back. Final Price Tenders will only be scaled
back (see Section&nbsp;1.17) if the Buy-Back Price is set at a 14&nbsp;per cent discount to the Market Price and the total number of Shares tendered at that discount and as Final Price Tenders is more than BHP Billiton Limited determines to buy
back. Therefore, if you wish to increase the likelihood that your Shares will be bought back, you may consider submitting a Final Price Tender.
</FONT></P></DIV><div style="clear:both; height:0px; font-size:0px">&nbsp;</div>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>1. Details of the Buy-Back and tender process
<FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="1">continued </FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"> </FONT></B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="font-size:12px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="line-height:2px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:2px;border-bottom:2pt solid #000000">&nbsp;</P> <p STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<DIV STYLE="position:relative;float:left; margin-right:1%; width:48%;padding-right:9px;padding-bottom:8px;overflow:hidden">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="tx157732_16"></A>1.13 How will I know what the Buy-Back Price is? </B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">BHP Billiton Limited intends to announce the Buy-Back Price to the ASX (and other relevant exchanges) as soon as practicable after the Tender Period
closes. BHP Billiton Limited expects this announcement to be on Monday, 11&nbsp;April 2011. The announcement will also be posted on BHP Billiton&#146;s website <B>(</B><B><I>www.bhpbilliton.com</I></B><B>)</B>. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="tx157732_17"></A>1.14 Will all the Shares I tender be bought back? </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The success of your Tender will depend on your Tender Discount, the size and price of Tenders lodged by other BHP Billiton Limited shareholders and the total number of Tenders that BHP Billiton Limited
accepts. There is no guarantee that all or even some of your Tender will be accepted. The final size of the Buy-Back will depend on tenders lodged by BHP Billiton Limited shareholders and market conditions. In particular, BHP Billiton Limited may
buy back significantly less than the announced target of A$5 billion, or no Shares at all. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="tx157732_18"></A>1.15 How will I know
how many of my Shares have been bought back? </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">No later than Monday, 18&nbsp;April 2011, BHP Billiton Limited will send all eligible BHP
Billiton Limited shareholders who have tendered their Shares into the Buy-Back a statement notifying them of the number of their Shares (if any) that have been bought back and the price paid. Eligible BHP Billiton Limited shareholders can also
access this information on or after Monday, 11&nbsp;April 2011 by calling the Buy-Back enquiry line on 1300 612 584 within Australia, 0800 451 521 within New Zealand or &#43;61 3 9415 4868 if you are calling from outside Australia or New Zealand. If
you are a CHESS Holder, you will receive written confirmation from CHESS of your Tenders that were successful made on your holding or Tenders withdrawn by your controlling participant. Shareholders may also enquire through the Registry website
<B>(</B><B><I>www.investorcentre.com</I></B><B>)</B> on or after Monday, 11&nbsp;April 2011. To access your account in Investor Centre you will need your Holder Identification Number (HIN) or Securityholder Reference Number (SRN).
</FONT></P></DIV><DIV STYLE="position:relative;float:right; width:48%;padding-right:9px;padding-bottom:8px;overflow:hidden">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="tx157732_19"></A>1.16 How will BHP Billiton Limited determine successful Tenders and any scale
back? </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">If BHP Billiton Limited proceeds with the Buy-Back and your Tender Discount is equal to or larger than the Buy-Back Discount, or you
lodged a Final Price Tender, your Tender will be successful and your Shares will be bought back, subject to any scale back and, if applicable, any Minimum Price condition. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">If your Tender Discount is smaller than the Buy-Back Discount, your Tender will be rejected and your Shares will not be bought back. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">If you have chosen a Minimum Price and the Buy-Back Price is below that price, your Tender will be rejected and your Shares will not be bought back. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="tx157732_20"></A>1.17 When may a scale back apply? </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">A scale back may apply if the total amount of Shares tendered at a Tender Discount, which is equal to or greater than the Buy-Back Discount, and as Final Price Tenders, is more than the total amount of
Shares that BHP Billiton Limited determines to buy back. In such circumstances, a scale back would apply as follows: </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>If the Buy-Back
Discount is between 10&nbsp;per cent and 13&nbsp;per cent (inclusive) </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Where the Buy-Back Discount is between 10&nbsp;per cent and
13&nbsp;per cent (inclusive): </FONT></P> <P STYLE="font-size:6px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Where the Buy-Back Discount is 14&nbsp;per cent: </FONT></P> <P STYLE="font-size:6px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P>

shareholder tendered Shares equal to or less than the Priority Allocation at a 14&nbsp;per cent Tender Discount or as a Final Price Tender, then all of those Shares will be bought back; </FONT></TD></TR></TABLE>

STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">When the scale back is calculated, all fractions will be rounded down to the nearest Share. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">If
you want to reduce the likelihood of any scale back applying to your Tender, you may consider submitting a Final Price Tender (see Section&nbsp;1.12 for further details). This is because in the event that a scale back applies, Shares tendered as a
Final Price Tender will only be scaled back if the Buy-Back Price is based on a 14&nbsp;per cent Tender Discount. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="tx157732_21"></A>1.18 What is the Priority Allocation? </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In the event of a scale back, BHP Billiton Limited will buy back the first 125 Shares successfully tendered by each shareholder or such lesser number of Shares determined to be the Priority Allocation as
is required to ensure that BHP Billiton Limited buys back only the number of Shares it determines to buy back. If you successfully tender less than the Priority Allocation, then all of your tendered Shares would be bought back as your Priority
Allocation in the circumstances described above. BHP Billiton Limited is offering the Priority Allocation to ensure that small eligible BHP Billiton Limited shareholders are not disadvantaged by any scale back.
</FONT></P></DIV><DIV STYLE="position:relative;float:right; width:48%;padding-right:9px;padding-bottom:8px;overflow:hidden">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="tx157732_22"></A>1.19 What is a Small Holding Tender? </B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">A Small Holding Tender is a Tender submitted by a BHP Billiton Limited shareholder who tenders all of their Shares at one or more Tender Discounts equal
to or greater than the Buy-Back Discount and/or as a Final Price Tender and who would have a Small Holding (50 Shares or less) created as a result of BHP Billiton Limited&#146;s acquisition of a Priority Allocation and any scale back. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">However, if you become the registered holder of additional ordinary shares in BHP Billiton Limited after the Buy-Back Record Date and, as a result, you
are the registered holder of more BHP Billiton Limited ordinary shares at the Closing Date than you held on the Buy-Back Record Date, then your Tender will not be a Small Holding Tender and the scale back will apply to your Tender as it would to any
other Tender. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="tx157732_23"></A>1.20 How would a scale back affect my Tender? </B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The details of any scale back will be announced as soon as possible after the Closing Date. BHP Billiton Limited expects to make this announcement on
Monday, 11&nbsp;April 2011. To assist you in understanding how a scale back may affect your Tender, the following two illustrative examples have been provided. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Examples </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">As an illustration, it is assumed that five eligible BHP Billiton Limited
shareholders with various sized holdings each tender Shares into the Buy-Back. In each of the two different examples: </FONT></P> <P STYLE="font-size:6px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Buy-Back Discount (and corresponding Buy-Back Price) and the scale back percentage are varied; but </FONT></P></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Shareholder A</B> chose Tender Discounts that are smaller than the Buy-Back Discount so no Shares would be bought back. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Shareholder B </B>tendered all of their 150 Shares as a Final Price Tender. The Tender would be successful and all 150 Shares would be bought back at
the Buy-Back Price of A$38.70. This is a Small Holding Tender as following the Priority Allocation of 125 Shares and scale back, Shareholder B would be left with 13 Shares (50 per cent of the remaining 25 Shares). When the scale back is calculated,
all fractions will be rounded down to the nearest Share. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Shareholder C</B> tendered all of their 6,000 Shares as a Final Price Tender. The
Final Price Tender would be partially successful as a result of the Priority Allocation and the 50&nbsp;per cent scale back, Shareholder C would have 3,062 Shares bought back. This is not a Small Holding Tender, as following the Priority Allocation
and scale back, Shareholder C would be left with more than 50 Shares (see scale back table below). </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Shareholder D</B> tendered 200 Shares
at a 12&nbsp;per cent Tender Discount and 4,000 Shares at a 14&nbsp;per cent Tender Discount. The Tender submitted at a 12&nbsp;per cent Tender Discount would not be successful as it is smaller than the 14&nbsp;per cent Buy-Back Discount. The Tender
submitted at a 14&nbsp;per cent Tender Discount would be successful but only 2,062 of the 4,000 Shares tendered would be bought back, as a result of the Priority Allocation and the 50&nbsp;per cent scale back (see scale back table below). This is
not a Small Holding Tender, as after accounting for the Priority Allocation and scale back, Shareholder D would be left with more than 50 Shares. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Shareholder E</B> tendered 200 Shares at a 12&nbsp;per cent Tender Discount. The Tender would not be successful as the 12&nbsp;per cent Tender Discount is smaller than the 14&nbsp;per cent Buy-Back
Discount. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Example 1: Scale back table (illustrative example only) </I></B></FONT></P>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="1"><SUP STYLE="vertical-align:baseline; position:relative; bottom:.8ex"></SUP></FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Under the Priority
Allocation, the first 125 Shares are bought back from each shareholder who tenders Shares at the Buy-Back Discount (including Shares tendered as a Final Price Tender under this example), before the scale back applies. For example, Shareholder C has
5,875 Shares that are subject to scale back (6,000 &#150; 125 = 5,875). </FONT></P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:6px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Shareholder A</B> tendered 5,000 Shares at a 10&nbsp;per cent Tender Discount and 5,000 Shares at a 12&nbsp;per cent Tender Discount. The Tender
submitted at a 10&nbsp;per cent Tender Discount would not be successful as this Tender Discount is smaller than the Buy-Back Discount. The Tender submitted at a 12&nbsp;per cent Tender Discount (A$39.60) would be successful but only 3,781 of the
5,000 Shares tendered would be bought back as a result of the Priority Allocation and the 25&nbsp;per cent scale back (see scale back table below). This is not a Small Holding Tender as Shareholder A did not tender all of their Shares at greater
than or equal to the Buy-Back Discount and, in any event, Shareholder A was not left with 50 Shares or less after the Priority Allocation and scale back. <B> </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Shareholder B</B> tendered all of their 150 Shares as a Final Price Tender. All 150 Shares tendered would be bought back at the Buy-Back Price of A$39.60, as Final Price Tenders are not subject to
scale back where the Buy-Back Discount (i.e. 12&nbsp;per cent) is not the largest Tender Discount of 14&nbsp;per cent. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Shareholder C</B>
tendered all of their 6,000 Shares as a Final Price Tender. All 6,000 Shares would be bought back at the Buy-Back Price of A$39.60. There will not be any scale back because the Buy-Back Discount is not the largest Tender Discount of 14&nbsp;per
cent. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Shareholder D</B> tendered a total of 4,200 Shares at two different Tender Discounts: 200 Shares at a 12&nbsp;per cent Tender
Discount and 4,000 Shares at a 14&nbsp;per cent Tender Discount. The Tender submitted at a 14&nbsp;per cent Tender Discount would be successful as 14&nbsp;per cent is greater than the Buy-Back Discount and all 4,000 Shares would be bought back at
A$39.60. The Tender submitted at a 12&nbsp;per cent Tender Discount would be successful and all 200 Shares would be bought back as it is a Small Holding Tender (see scale back table below). This is a Small Holding Tender since after the Priority
Allocation and scale back are applied, Shareholder D would be left with 50 Shares or less. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Shareholder E</B> tendered 200 of their Shares
at a 12&nbsp;per cent Tender Discount. The Tender would be partially successful and 181 Shares would be bought back (see scale back table below). This is not a Small Holding Tender since Shareholder E did not tender all of their Shares at greater
than or equal to the Buy-Back Discount and/or as a Final Price Tender. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Example 2: Scale back table (illustrative example only)
</I></B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="font-size:12px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font-size:12px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P><DIV STYLE="position:relative;float:left; margin-right:1%; width:48%;padding-right:9px;padding-bottom:8px;overflow:hidden">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="tx157732_24"></A>1.21 Can I elect a Minimum Price for the purchase of my Shares?
</B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">If you choose to tender Shares into the Buy-Back, you will need to nominate a Tender Discount or lodge a Final Price Tender. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">If you are concerned that movements in the Market Price after you lodge your Tender may result in your Tender corresponding to a lower Buy-Back Price
than you are willing to sell your Shares for, then you have the option of making your Tender conditional on the Buy-Back Price being no less than a specified Minimum Price. Note that this may affect the success of your Tender because if the Buy-Back
Price is below your Minimum Price, then your Tender will be rejected and your Shares will not be bought back. If you choose to make your Tender conditional on the Buy-Back Price being no less than one of the specified Minimum Prices, you must do
this in addition to nominating a Tender Discount or a Final Price Tender. If you fail to nominate a Tender Discount or a Final Price Tender, and only make your Tender conditional on a specified Minimum Price, your Tender will be invalid and will not
be accepted by BHP Billiton Limited. </FONT></P></DIV><DIV STYLE="position:relative;float:right; width:48%;padding-right:9px;padding-bottom:8px;overflow:hidden">

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="tx157732_26"></A>1.23 How do I participate in the Buy-Back? Step 1 &#150; Decide how many
Shares you wish to sell </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">To participate in the Buy-Back, you first need to decide how many Shares you wish to sell. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The personalised Tender Form enclosed with this booklet sets out the maximum number of Shares you may tender into the Buy-Back. However, if you hold 125
Shares or less, to participate you must tender all of your Shares and if you hold more than 125 Shares, you must tender a minimum of 125 Shares in aggregate. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>You should not, before the Buy-Back Date, sell or offer to sell to others the Shares you have tendered into the Buy-Back unless you first withdraw or amend your Tender (see Section&nbsp;1.24).
</B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Step 2 &#150; Choose your Tender Discount(s) and/or a Final Price Tender </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Once you have determined the number of Shares you wish to tender into the Buy-Back, you need to specify the discount(s) to the Market Price at which you are willing to tender these Shares (your Tender
Discount(s)). </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">You may tender your Shares at discounts of between 10&nbsp;per cent and 14&nbsp;per cent inclusive (at 1&nbsp;per cent
intervals) to the Market Price as set out on the Tender Form or as a Final Price Tender. If you hold 125 Shares or less, to participate you must tender all of your Shares at the same Tender Discount or as a Final Price Tender (which is an election
to receive the </FONT></P></DIV><DIV STYLE="position:relative;float:right; width:48%;padding-right:9px;padding-bottom:8px;overflow:hidden">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">
Buy-Back Price, whatever BHP Billiton Limited determines it to be). But if you hold more than 125 Shares, you may tender different parcels of the Shares you wish to sell at different Tender
Discounts. For example, you may tender one third of the Shares you wish to sell at a 14&nbsp;per cent Tender Discount, one third at a 10&nbsp;per cent Tender Discount and one third as a Final Price Tender. However, you may not tender the same Shares
at different Tender Discounts (or at both a specified Tender Discount and as a Final Price Tender). Each parcel of Shares tendered at a different Tender Discount or as a Final Price Tender is a separate Tender (but entered on the one form). The
total number of Shares that you tender into the Buy-Back must not exceed the number set out in Box A on your Tender Form. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">To provide an
indication of the Market Price, BHP Billiton will calculate and make available to eligible shareholders the running VWAP during the five-day period as referred to in Section&nbsp;1.11. The running VWAP will be published on BHP Billiton&#146;s
website (<B><I>www.bhpbilliton.com</I></B>) from approximately 6.00pm (Melbourne time) on Monday, 4&nbsp;April 2011 and will be available through the Buy-Back enquiry line from Tuesday, 5&nbsp;April 2011 and will be updated cumulatively each day.
Please note that the Market Price information provided by BHP Billiton on its website and through the Buy-Back enquiry line will only be an estimate given that it is a cumulative daily update from opening of trading on Monday, 4&nbsp;April 2011.
</FONT></P></DIV><div style="clear:both; height:0px; font-size:0px">&nbsp;</div>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>1. Details of the Buy-Back and tender process
<FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="1">continued</FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"> </FONT></B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="font-size:12px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="line-height:2px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:2px;border-bottom:2pt solid #000000">&nbsp;</P> <p STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<DIV STYLE="position:relative;float:left; margin-right:1%; width:48%;padding-right:9px;padding-bottom:8px;overflow:hidden">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The actual Market Price, representing the VWAP for the full five-day period up to and including the Closing
Date, will be available from approximately 6.00pm (Melbourne time) on Friday, 8&nbsp;April 2011, and can be obtained by accessing the BHP Billiton website or by calling the Buy-Back enquiry line on 1300 612 584 within Australia, 0800 451 521 within
New Zealand or &#43;61 3 9415 4868 if you are calling from outside Australia or New Zealand. BHP Billiton Limited also intends to announce the Market Price to the ASX (and other relevant exchanges) as soon as practicable on Friday, 8&nbsp;April
2011. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">BHP Billiton Limited shareholders may wish to delay submitting their Tender until towards the end of the Tender Period so that they can
consider the approximate Market Price before submitting their Tender Form. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Step 3 &#150; Optional &#150; choose your Minimum Price
</B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In addition to choosing to tender your Shares at the specified Tender Discounts and/or as a Final Price Tender, you may also elect to
impose a Minimum Price condition on your Tender (see Section&nbsp;1.21). </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Step 4 &#150; Submit your Tender(s) </B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">How you submit your Tender(s) will depend on the type of holding you have. The method for submitting your Tenders will be specified on your Tender Form.
</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>(a) Issuer Sponsored Holdings </I></B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Once you have determined the number of Shares you wish to tender into the Buy-Back and your Tender Discount(s) and/or Final Price Tender, and, if you choose, your Minimum Price, you need to complete and
sign your personalised Tender Form and return it to the Registry by 7.00pm (Melbourne time) on Friday, 8&nbsp;April 2011: </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>If sending by
mail </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">BHP Billiton Limited Buy-Back </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">C/- Computershare Investor Services Pty Limited </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">GPO Box 52 </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Melbourne VIC 8060 </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">AUSTRALIA </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>If sending by facsimile </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">BHP Billiton
Limited Buy-Back </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Fax no: &#43;61 3 9473 2092 </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">You can use the enclosed reply-paid envelope if you are posting your Tender Form from within Australia. If you are sending your Tender Form by facsimile, do NOT send your original Tender Form to the
Registry. </FONT></P></DIV><DIV STYLE="position:relative;float:right; width:48%;padding-right:9px;padding-bottom:8px;overflow:hidden">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">BHP Billiton Limited will not accept your Tender Form unless it is actually received at the specified
address before the Tender Period closes. You should allow sufficient time for your Tender Form to be received if you are sending your Tender Form by mail. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>(b) CHESS Holdings </I></B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Once you have determined the number of Shares you wish to sell,
your Tender Discount(s) and/or Final Price Tenders, and, if you choose, your Minimum Price, you need to instruct your controlling participant (normally your broker) in sufficient time for them to process your Tender so that it is received by the
Registry by 7.00pm (Melbourne time) on Friday, 8&nbsp;April 2011. The name of the controlling participant who manages your CHESS Holding as at the Buy-Back Record Date is printed on your Tender Form. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">You should NOT send your Tender Form to the Registry. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">If you are a CHESS Holder, you will be sent written confirmation from CHESS of the Tenders made on your holding or Tenders withdrawn by your controlling participant. Irrespective of its wording, this
confirmation is not an acceptance by BHP Billiton Limited of any Tender. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="tx157732_27"></A>1.24 Can I withdraw or amend my Tender?
</B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Once you have submitted a Tender, it can only be withdrawn or amended by following the procedures set out below. </FONT></P>

withdraw or amend a Tender that has been received by the Registry, you will need to submit a Withdrawal/ Amendment Form, a copy of which is included at the back of this booklet. If you wish to withdraw all of your Tenders (&#145;Withdrawal&#146;),
or change the terms of all or some of your Tenders, or withdraw some (not all) of your Tenders (&#145;Amendment&#146;), you must follow the following procedure: </FONT></P> <P STYLE="font-size:6px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="tx157732_33"></A>2 Australian tax implications for BHP Billiton Limited shareholders
</B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="font-size:12px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="line-height:2px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:2px;border-bottom:2pt solid #000000">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>The following discussion is intended only as a general summary of the Australian income tax implications of participating in the Buy-Back </B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="font-size:12px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="line-height:2px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:2px;border-bottom:2pt solid #000000">&nbsp;
</P><DIV STYLE="position:relative;float:left; margin-right:1%; width:48%;padding-right:9px;padding-bottom:8px;overflow:hidden">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B></B>If you decide to participate in the Buy-Back, your particular tax treatment will depend on your own
circumstances. <B>It is therefore important that you seek professional tax advice to take into account your particular circumstances. </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="tx157732_34">
</A>2.1 Introduction </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Unless otherwise specified, this discussion is based on Australian income tax legislation and administrative practice
as at 24&nbsp;February 2011. These laws, the interpretation of them by the courts, and administrative practice may change at any time, and sometimes with retrospective effect. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In May 2009, the Assistant Treasurer announced a number of proposed changes to the tax laws affecting off-market share buy-backs. These changes, if enacted, may affect the terms on which companies offer
to buy back their shares and the taxation consequences for BHP Billiton Limited shareholders of participating in a buy-back. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">It has been
announced that any changes to the taxation laws affecting off-market share buy-backs would apply from the date of enactment of the relevant legislation. Since that legislation has yet to be introduced into Parliament, BHP Billiton Limited does not
anticipate that the Buy-Back will be affected by the proposed changes, but this cannot be known with certainty. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="font-size:12px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;
</FONT></P></DIV><DIV STYLE="position:relative;float:right; width:48%;padding-right:9px;padding-bottom:8px;overflow:hidden">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">BHP Billiton Limited has received a draft Class Ruling from the ATO for BHP Billiton Limited shareholders
who participate in the Buy-Back, which provides preliminary confirmation of a number of the statements contained in this summary. The ATO will not issue the Class Ruling in a form that is binding until after completion of the Buy-Back. Although it
is not anticipated to be the case, when the binding Class Ruling is issued by the ATO, it is possible that it may express a view contrary to that set out below. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">This general summary of the Australian income tax implications of participating in the Buy-Back is limited to BHP Billiton Limited shareholders who hold their Shares on capital account and therefore may
be assessed for tax under the capital gains tax (&#145;CGT&#146;) provisions on Shares bought back by BHP Billiton Limited. BHP Billiton Limited shareholders who: </FONT></P> <P STYLE="font-size:6px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>2. Australian tax implications for BHP Billiton Limited shareholders <FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="1">continued </FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"> </FONT></B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="font-size:12px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="line-height:2px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:2px;border-bottom:2pt solid #000000">&nbsp;</P> <p STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<DIV STYLE="position:relative;float:left; margin-right:1%; width:48%;padding-right:9px;padding-bottom:8px;overflow:hidden">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="tx157732_35"></A>2.2 Income tax &#150; Treatment of Dividend Component of Buy-Back Price
</B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Australian Resident Shareholders </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>What proportion of the Buy-Back Price is a deemed dividend that I must include in my assessable income? </I></B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Buy-Back will constitute an &#145;off-market&#146; buy-back for the purposes of Division 16K of Part III of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1936. It is anticipated that the Capital Component of the
Buy-Back Price will be A$0.28 and that all of the Buy-Back Price in excess of A$0.28 (Dividend Component) will be treated as a frankable distribution. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Dividend Component will be fully franked. You will need to include this amount in your assessable income. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Will I be entitled to a tax offset? </I></B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">If you are entitled to the benefit of franking
credits on the Dividend Component (see section entitled &#145;Franking Credit Entitlements&#146; below) you will also: </FONT></P> <P STYLE="font-size:6px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR>
<TD WIDTH="12" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#149;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1" VALIGN="top"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">need to include the franking credit on the Dividend Component in your assessable income; and </FONT></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="font-size:6px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR>
<TD WIDTH="12" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#149;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1" VALIGN="top"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">be entitled to a tax offset equal to the franking credit. </FONT></P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The tax offset may reduce the total tax payable on your taxable income. If you are an individual or a complying superannuation entity and your total tax offsets exceed the total tax payable on your
taxable income, you may be entitled to a cash refund of that excess. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Generally no refunds will be available to companies if the tax offset
exceeds the tax payable, however, they may be able to carry forward any excess tax offsets to reduce tax payable in future income years. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Will an Australian resident company be entitled to a credit in its own franking account? </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Yes. If the company satisfies the holding period rules (see section entitled &#145;Franking Credit Entitlements&#146; below), the company should enter the franking credit in its franking account and it
can be used to frank dividends that the company pays. </FONT></P></DIV><DIV STYLE="position:relative;float:right; width:48%;padding-right:9px;padding-bottom:8px;overflow:hidden">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Non-Resident Shareholders </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>What is the tax treatment if I am not a resident of Australia? </I></B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">If you are a
non-resident shareholder that does not carry on business through a permanent establishment in Australia, the Dividend Component is not subject to either Australian income tax or Australian withholding tax as it will be fully franked. The franking
credits which are attached to the Dividend Component will generally have no further relevance for you and no part of those franking credits is refundable by the ATO to you. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Different consequences may arise if you hold Shares as part of a business conducted through a permanent establishment in Australia. In that case, you should obtain your own Australian tax advice before
making a decision to participate in the Buy-Back. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The treatment of the Dividend Component as a deemed dividend is a function of Australian
tax law (Division 16K of Part III of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1936) and does not alter the fact that, for all other purposes, the Buy-Back Price is the proceeds from selling the shares back to BHP Billiton Limited. It cannot therefore be
assumed that the tax laws of the jurisdiction in which you reside will treat any part of the Buy-Back Price as a dividend. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Franking Credit
Entitlements </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Are there any rules which might deny me the benefit of the franking credits? </I></B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Australian tax legislation includes a number of rules which may prevent you from claiming the benefit of franking credits on the Dividend Component.
These rules are designed to, amongst other things, discourage trading in franking credits. These rules may deny the benefit of franking credits to you generally, or because of your particular circumstances.
</FONT></P></DIV><div style="clear:both; height:0px; font-size:0px">&nbsp;</div>

<DIV STYLE="position:relative;float:left; margin-right:1%; width:48%;padding-right:9px;padding-bottom:8px;overflow:hidden">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Will the anti-streaming rules deny me the benefit of franking credits? </I></B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">BHP Billiton Limited has received preliminary advice from the ATO that it will not make a determination to deny participating BHP Billiton Limited
shareholders the benefit of franking credits on the Dividend Component. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">However, the particular circumstances of each participating
shareholder will also be relevant in determining whether the rules deny the benefit of the tax offset or franking credit. For example, the period during which you hold the Shares and any arrangements you have in relation to the Shares will be
important. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>How long do I have to hold the Shares to be entitled to the franking credits? </I></B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">To qualify for the franking credit on the Dividend Component you must be a &#145;qualified person&#146;. You will be a qualified person if: </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="font-size:6px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR>
<TD WIDTH="12" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#149;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1" VALIGN="top"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">you satisfy one of the specific concessions in the legislation (for example, you are an individual whose total franking credit entitlement for the
income year does not exceed A$5,000); or </FONT></P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:6px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR>
<TD WIDTH="12" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#149;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1" VALIGN="top"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">you satisfy the &#145;45-day rule&#146;. </FONT></P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The 45-day rule requires that if you are an Australian resident shareholder you have to have held your Shares &#145;at risk&#146; for a period of at least 45 days excluding the days of acquisition and
disposal. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The 45-day rule is complex. Generally, if you are subject to the rule and you acquired all of your Shares on or before Thursday,
24&nbsp;February 2011 you will have held your shares for 45 clear days in respect of the Dividend Component. This is on the assumption that the determination of the Buy-Back allocations occurs on Monday, 11&nbsp;April 2011.
</FONT></P></DIV><DIV STYLE="position:relative;float:right; width:48%;padding-right:9px;padding-bottom:8px;overflow:hidden">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Will I have held my shares at risk over this 45-day period? </I></B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">You can still not satisfy the 45-day rule even if you acquired your Shares on or before Thursday, 24&nbsp;February 2011. This may arise where you have
entered into other arrangements regarding the Shares, which reduce the risk of loss or opportunity for gain on the Shares. For example, granting an option to another person to acquire the Shares would reduce that risk or opportunity. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In addition, if you are under an obligation to make a payment that passes the benefit of the Dividend Component to another person, you may also not
qualify for the franking credit unless other &#145;at risk&#146; holding requirements are satisfied. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>If I acquire shares after the
ex-entitlement date will this impact Shares tendered into the Buy-Back? </I></B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The 45-day rule operates on the last-in-first-out principle so
you will be deemed, for the purpose of applying the 45-day rule, to have disposed of your most recently acquired Shares under the Buy-Back. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The ATO generally accepts that shares purchased on or after the ex-entitlement date for an off-market buy-back (in this case, Shares purchased on or
after Friday, 25&nbsp;February 2011) will be excluded from the &#145;last-in-first-out&#146; rule. The acquisition of Shares on an ex-entitlement basis will therefore not affect your ability to receive franking credits on Shares acquired on or
before Thursday, 24&nbsp;February 2011 which are tendered into the Buy-Back. If the determination of the Buy-Back allocations occurs on a day other than Monday, 11&nbsp;April 2011, these dates may alter.
</FONT></P></DIV><div style="clear:both; height:0px; font-size:0px">&nbsp;</div>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px;padding-bottom:0px;"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="tx157732_36"></A>2.3 Capital Gains Tax (&#145;CGT&#146;) &#150; Disposal of

</FONT></B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Australian Resident Shareholders </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT

<P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>What is the Tax Value of the Shares? </I></B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT

Value should be determined as the volume weighted average price of the shares over the last five trading days before the first announcement of the buy-back, adjusted for the movement in the S&amp;P/ASX 200 Index from the opening of trading on the
announcement date to the close of trading on the day the buy-back closes. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">TD2004/22 also provides that if companies undertaking an off-market
share buy-back wish to vary this methodology, representations should be made to the ATO explaining the rationale for this variation. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">BHP
Billiton Limited has made representations to the ATO that the market value setting methodology adopted in TD2004/22 should be varied in determining the Tax Value of Shares. As a result of these representations, the ATO has indicated that for the

However, in light of the size of the Capital Component, this will not typically occur. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Under current law, you will make a capital loss for a
Share disposed of under the Buy-Back if the CGT cost base of the Share exceeds the Capital Proceeds. No allowance for indexation or non-capital costs is made in determining the CGT cost base of the Share in calculating a capital loss.

 <P STYLE="font-size:12px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="line-height:2px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:2px;border-bottom:2pt solid #000000">&nbsp;</P>
<p STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<DIV STYLE="position:relative;float:left; margin-right:1%; width:48%;padding-right:9px;padding-bottom:8px;overflow:hidden">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The capital loss which arises under the Buy-Back may be greater than the capital loss which may have arisen
under an equivalent sale of the Shares on-market. This is because the Capital Proceeds under the Buy-Back are limited to A$0.28 plus the amount (if any) by which the Tax Value exceeds the Buy-Back Price, rather than the price at which the
shareholder would have sold their Shares on-market. The lower Capital Proceeds also mean that any capital gain which may otherwise have arisen on disposal of the Shares under the Buy-Back is reduced or eliminated. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">If you are a company, or normally taxed as a company, it does not necessarily follow that you will have a capital loss if the Capital Proceeds are less
than the CGT cost base of the share (excluding indexation and non-capital costs). Where a shareholder is a company, or is normally taxed as a company, the amount of any capital loss is reduced by the lesser of: </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="font-size:6px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR>
<TD WIDTH="12" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#149;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1" VALIGN="top"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">the fully franked Dividend Component; and </FONT></P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:6px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR>
<TD WIDTH="12" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#149;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1" VALIGN="top"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">the amount of the capital loss. </FONT></P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">If a capital loss does arise from the Buy-Back, you cannot offset that capital loss or any part of it against the Dividend Component or any franking credit included in your assessable income, as it can
only be used to offset capital gains. Capital losses that are not used in the income year in which they arise may usually be carried forward and used to offset capital gains made in later income years. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Section&nbsp;2.4 provides illustrative examples of the potential tax consequences for an Australian resident individual disposing of their Shares under
the Buy-Back. The actual tax consequences will depend on the Buy-Back Price, the Tax Value, the individual&#146;s applicable marginal tax rate and their CGT cost base for the Shares.
</FONT></P></DIV><DIV STYLE="position:relative;float:right; width:48%;padding-right:9px;padding-bottom:8px;overflow:hidden">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Will I receive a CGT discount? </I></B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">If you have held your Shares for more than 12 months prior to the date of disposal (anticipated to be Monday, 11&nbsp;April 2011), you are eligible for the discount and need only include in your
assessable income one-half (for individuals) and two-thirds (for complying superannuation funds) of any net capital gain. If you are a company you are not entitled to any CGT discount. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>What will be my CGT cost base? </I></B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Generally, the CGT cost base for a Share will be the
amount that you paid to acquire the Share together with certain incidental costs of acquisition, for example stamp duty and brokerage, and certain incidental costs of disposal. If you are the trustee of a superannuation fund, you should note that
the cost base of shares acquired before 1&nbsp;July 1988 may be adjusted to the market value of the shares on 30&nbsp;June 1988. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">If you
acquired your Shares pursuant to an employee equity scheme, your cost base will be determined under the specific provisions dealing with such schemes. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The cost base must also be adjusted for any capital reductions or bonus issues of shares. For example, on the formation of the DLC in 2001 a bonus issue of 1.0651 shares for each share held was made.
Further, capital reductions were undertaken to facilitate the demerger of each of OneSteel Ltd in October 2000 (A$0.66 per share reduction in the cost base per share before adjustment for DLC bonus shares) and BlueScope Steel Ltd in July 2002 (5.063
per cent reduction in cost base per share). </FONT></P></DIV><div style="clear:both; height:0px; font-size:0px">&nbsp;</div>

 <p STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">22 </FONT></P>



<p Style='page-break-before:always'>
